jobs.description:
Alliance for Audited Media seeking an experienced Vice President, Technology who will be responsible for the leadership and management of the organization's technology infrastructure, cybersecurity, enterprise applications, software development, and IT operations. This primarily position reports to the Chief Financial Officer/ Chief Operating Officer. This position leads the planning and execution of strategic technology initiatives and is accountable for technology investments and outcomes, while ensuring reliable, secure, and cost-effective technology services that support the organization's business objectives.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS OF THE JOB

Lead the technology function and establish technology priorities and direction in partnership with executive leadership and in alignment with organizational goals, business needs, and strategic objectives.

Establish and maintain an effective technology governance framework for evaluating, prioritizing, and overseeing technology initiatives, investments, and resources.

Develop and manage the annual IT operating and capital budgets, including technology forecasting, resource planning, and evaluation of proposed technology investments.

Oversee the organization's technology platforms, business applications, infrastructure, and systems, including evaluation, modernization, integration, and lifecycle management.

Oversee cybersecurity, technology risk management, data protection, and related controls to safeguard organizational information and technology resources.

Manage enterprise infrastructure, including Microsoft 365, Azure, AWS, virtualization, servers, networking, backup, and disaster recovery.

Recommend and implement cost-effective technology solutions that ensure secure, reliable, and high-performing systems.

Oversee IT operations, help desk support, and relationships with technology vendors, contractors, and managed service providers, including contract performance and service delivery.

Supervise IT staff by providing leadership, mentoring, coaching, staff development and succession planning, and performance management.

Lead knowledge transfer and documentation efforts to preserve institutional knowledge, strengthen  business continuity, and reduce operational dependency.

Develop and maintain IT policies, procedures, documentation, and technology standards.

Serve as a strategic technology advisor to executive leadership, communicating technology priorities, investments, risks, opportunities, and results in support of informed business decisions.

Evaluate emerging technologies and industry practices and recommend solutions that improve organizational effectiveness, security, reliability, and operational efficiency.

OTHER KEY JOB FUNCTIONS

Collaborate with department leaders to identify opportunities for process improvement through technology.
Support enterprise data management and reporting initiatives that improve business decision-making.
Participate in cross-functional projects and organizational initiatives as needed.
Maintain current knowledge of emerging technologies, cybersecurity trends, and industry best practices and apply that knowledge to support organizational technology planning and decision-making.
Present technology plans, risks, priorities, and initiatives to executive leadership as needed, and as requested, to the Board of Directors.
Perform other duties as assigned.

JOB SPECIFICATIONS

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or related field.
Minimum 10 years of progressive IT experience.
Minimum 5 years leading technical teams or enterprise IT projects.
Experience developing and executing technology strategies, governance practices, and technology investment priorities aligned with organizational objectives.
Experience managing technology vendors, contractors, and managed service providers, including contract negotiations, performance management, and service delivery.
Experience overseeing cloud platforms, infrastructure, networking, cybersecurity, data protection, and enterprise applications.
Experience leading application development or legacy system modernization, or cloud migration projects.
Strong knowledge of databases, systems integration, and enterprise technologies.
Excellent leadership, project management, vendor management, communication, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to communicate technical concepts effectively to executive leadership and non-technical stakeholders.
Experience with technologies such as Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics 365, Microsoft 365, Azure, AWS, or comparable enterprise platforms is preferred.
Experience with cybersecurity, data protection, business continuity, and disaster recovery practices is preferred.
Microsoft, Cisco, Azure, AWS, VMware, or related certifications preferred.

ENVIRONMENT:

Primarily remote work environment.
Periodic onsite presence at AAM's Schaumburg, Illinois office during the first nine months will be expected to support knowledge transfer and transition activities.
Occasional travel for company meetings, technology implementations, or vendor meetings as required.
Availability to work outside normal business hours during system implementations, maintenance windows, or emergency situations.

About Alliance for Audited Media

The Alliance for Audited Media is the industry’s assurance partner. Founded in 1914 by the Association of National Advertisers as the Audit Bureau of Circulations (ABC), AAM has evolved from verifying print circulation to providing assurance across the media and advertising ecosystem. In 2023, AAM merged with BPA Worldwide to become the largest not-for-profit media assurance organization governed by a board of directors representing agencies, marketers and publishers.

Our mission is to collaborate with the industry to set standards and develop assurance programs that bring greater transparency to channels including digital, print, retail media, events, out-of-home, ad tech and more.

Together with our members and partners, we are committed to setting universal benchmarks for media transparency, helping develop accountability solutions and promoting excellence that elevates the entire industry.

8+ years of software engineering experience with 3+ years leading and managing engineers (or equivalent combination of education and experience).
Strong React 18+ expertise (hooks, Suspense, StrictMode, error boundaries, lazy loading) and modern TypeScript patterns.
Deep experience with Webpack 5 and Module Federation or similar approaches to modular front-end architecture.
Experience designing and operating micro-frontend systems or other independently deployable UI architectures.
Solid experience integrating or developing backend services, including API design and microservices-based architectures.
Familiarity with event-driven communication patterns (pub/sub) and cross-module state management approaches.
Experience implementing or working with authentication and authorization patterns (e.g., JWT, RBAC).
Experience with CI/CD pipelines and modern development practices including testing and code quality standards.

Experience with accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1) and building inclusive user experiences.
Exposure to AI/LLM-powered UI experiences or developer productivity tools.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Market Solutions Engineering
jobs.description:
The New York Independent System Operator (NYISO) manages the efficient flow of electricity on more than 11,000 circuit-miles of high-voltage transmission lines, dispatching power from hundreds of generating units across the state.

The New York Independent System Operator (NYISO) applies cutting-edge technology to operating a reliable electricity system, managing competitive markets for wholesale electricity, and planning for the Empire State's energy future. The NYISO’s Market Structures department invites applications for a full-time Senior Manager, Market Solutions Engineering.

The Senior Manager, Market Solutions Engineering is responsible for setting technical direction and leading the research, market technology, production support, implementation, and external engagement functions that support NYISO’s energy, capacity, and TCC market systems. This position provides strategic leadership across Market Design, Market Operations, Grid Operations, Market Mitigation and Analysis, Information Technology, System & Resource Planning, and Product and Project Management to advance NYISO’s strategic initiatives and long-term market vision.

The Senior Manager leads the development and evolution of market technology solutions, oversees preliminary and feasibility simulation studies for future market products, and ensures market applications remain functional and aligned with market rules and reliability criteria. The role also directs projects that build upon the Energy Market System and Business Market System to support emerging resource technologies and New York State renewable integration objectives.

The position provides leadership for day-ahead and real-time energy market engineering support, production issue resolution, vendor and consultant engagement, implementation readiness, testing coordination, external research engagements, and ongoing technical support for market software and market participant inquiries.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES And RESPONSIBILITIES

Provide strategic leadership for Market Solutions Engineering and Market Research and Engineering teams, including research, prototype development, market technology strategy, implementation support, production support, and long-term market solution planning.
Lead collaboration with Market Design, Project and Product Management, Information Technology, Operations, Grid Operations, Market Mitigation and Analysis, System & Resource Planning, and other business areas through the full project lifecycle, from market design and requirements development through implementation, testing, deployment, and post-production support.
Direct engagement with vendors and consultants supporting NYISO production systems and market applications; review vendor-proposed solutions, provide direction on design notes development and ensure solutions align with market rules, operational needs, reliability criteria, and long-range market strategies.
Provide strategic direction to Grid Operations and Market Operations teams regarding production changes, market software enhancements, prioritization of improvements, and resolution of software issues encountered in day-ahead and real-time market operations.
Define, sponsor and lead studies of future market products and technologies using prototyping, simulations, historical data analysis, and other sound technical approaches to validate requirements, assess technical robustness, evaluate potential market outcomes and consumer impacts, identify market behavioral risks and confirm compliance objectives.
Present, explain and defend technical approaches, study results, implementation strategies and recommended solutions to senior management, stakeholders, vendors, and internal cross-functional teams.
Balance market operations and grid operations operational enhancements with NYISO’s long-term market plans and strategic planning priorities.
Lead the technical development of mathematical models and optimization-based solutions for energy, capacity, and TCC markets, including commitment, dispatch, pricing, resource adequacy modeling approaches to meet peak system demand and capacity accreditation factors used in resource adequacy models.
Administer and provide direction on software modifications to Security Constrained Unit Commitment, Real-Time Scheduling, unit commitment, dispatch and pricing programs, including enhancements related to MIP solution approaches, dynamic reserves procurement, account for constraint-specific transmission shortages, modeling generator duct firing operational limitations, participation models for Energy Storage Resources, Co-located Storage Resources, aggregation resources, distributed energy resources, large load participation models in wholesale electricity markets, scarcity pricing enhancements, external transaction pricing, and broader regional market initiatives.
Lead or coordinate proof-of-concept testing, user acceptance testing and implementation readiness activities for changes to core energy market algorithms and supporting market software.
Provide implementation support to product teams by reviewing requirements documents, reviewing and approving design notes, supporting user acceptance test plans, and ensuring enhancements and new features are ready for production deployment.
Oversee technical support to Market Monitoring, IT Quality Assurance, Stakeholder Services, Market Validation, and Operations for market participant questions, scheduling and pricing outcome validation, production investigations, and audit-related inquiries.
Support corporate SOC1 process and procedure audit principles by promoting best practices, periodic audit activities, traceable documentation, and disciplined production-support processes.
Direct, support, and maintain specialized operations and market-solution applications, including PMU applications, stand-alone visualization software, as applicable to the assigned functional portfolio.
Monitor FERC, regional ISO/RTO, academia, and industry developments; collaborate with other ISOs/RTOs on technology and business solution evaluation; and recommend technical and business evolution initiatives in coordination with NYISO senior management.
Represent NYISO on external industry advisory boards and in industry organizations such as PSERC, EPRI, CEATI, CIGRE, national labs, universities, and other research forums; participate in major national and international conferences and seminars.
Oversee external research engagements for NYISO, including active management of university and research organization collaborations, review of DOE, NSF, NYSERDA, and related proposals, and maintenance of an active research program aligned with NYISO market needs.
Supervise, train, develop, and mentor managers and professional staff supporting market solutions, research, software testing, market modeling, and implementation activities; establish priorities, develop talent, and build technical depth across the team.
Provide direction for teams that provide 24x7 on-call production support to resolve issues in a timely manner.

Supervisory Responsibilities

This position has supervisory responsibility and may have both managerial and non-supervisory employees reporting to the position. The role is expected to provide leadership, coaching, prioritization, and performance direction for technical staff and subordinate leaders supporting market solutions, research, modeling, testing, implementation, and production-support activities.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations Research, or another related technical field is required. Knowledge of Power Systems Engineering and Economics is preferred. A Master’s degree is strongly preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
A minimum of ten years of electrical engineering and/or software development experience is required, including technology leadership or supervisory experience in research, technology analysis, market systems, electric utilities, interconnected public service, or energy markets; or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.
Experience should include knowledge of power system operations, system planning, electricity markets, computer systems, optimization modeling, application software development, data engineering, scripting, and shell programming. For the senior manager role, demonstrated progressive leadership of complex market technology initiatives, cross-functional implementation teams, vendor relationships, external research engagements, and production support functions is expected.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

None required.

Additional Requirements

Excellent verbal, written, presentation, interpersonal, organizational, teamwork, and management skills.
Ability to read, analyze, and interpret scientific and technical journals, financial reports, legal documents, business periodicals, technical procedures, government regulations, and professional journals.
Ability to respond to inquiries or complaints from market participants, regulatory agencies, members of the business community, vendors, managers, and the public.
Ability to write reports, business correspondence, procedure manuals, speeches, articles, and materials that conform to prescribed style and format.
Ability to effectively present information to senior management, public groups, boards of directors, vendors, market participants, regulators, and cross-functional internal teams.
Ability to work with probability, statistical inference, advanced calculus, modern algebra, advanced statistical theory, geometry, trigonometry, optimization concepts, fractions, percentages, ratios, and proportions, and to apply these concepts to practical situations.
Ability to define problems, collect and analyze data, establish facts, draw valid conclusions, interpret complex technical instructions, and apply logical or scientific thinking to abstract and concrete problems.
Advanced competency in Linux operating systems, shell programming including Sed and Awk, scripting languages such as Python, optimization modeling primarily in AMPL or GAMS, and fine-tuning solution tolerances in commercial solvers such as Gurobi or CPLEX.
Intermediate competency in Windows operating environments using Microsoft Office applications, e-mail, and internet programs.
Knowledge and understanding of market software, market software development processes, IT software development practices, project lifecycle activities, and production support disciplines.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to stand, walk, sit, and use hands to perform routine office tasks. The employee is occasionally required to reach with hands and arms. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 15 pounds. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Contact with staff and the public will occur. Travel may be required to attend and/or conduct meetings, conferences, and training. This position may require work on nights, weekends, or holidays.

At the NYISO, we realize the importance of balancing the availability of remote work with the inherent value of bringing people together to attain success in the areas of maximum collaboration, relationship building and growth, teamwork, innovation and problem solving, as well as professional development and mentoring. In this role, you will be required to work onsite from our Rensselaer, NY location several days per workweek, with the option to work remotely on the remaining days. You will also be expected to respond to all business needs that may require any increase to the regular onsite requirements.

The NYISO takes pride in recruiting, developing and retaining highly talented individuals. In addition to competitive salaries,

new_jobs.title: Director/Principal Engineer, Data & AI Platform
new_jobs.description:
About Arlo

At Arlo, we're passionate about creating innovative and reliable solutions that help people protect what matters most to them. Our team is dedicated to delivering products that exceed our customers' expectations, while always pushing the boundaries of what's possible in the world of protection technology. We believe that everyone deserves to feel safe and secure, whether they're at home or away, and we're committed to providing our customers with the peace of mind they need to live their lives without worry. Arlo’s deep expertise in AI- and CV-powered analytics, cloud services, user experience, product design, and innovative wireless and RF connectivity enables the delivery of a seamless, smart security experience for Arlo users that is easy to set up and interact with every day.

About The Role

Arlo is looking for a senior technical leader to turn our data platform into an AI-native internal product — one with real consumers, a clear owner, and a roadmap.

The Difference This Role Makes Should Be Measurable

Any team at Arlo can find a trusted metric or dataset without asking around.

New data products get built on shared primitives instead of from scratch.

Dashboards get retired because a governed, self-service version replaced them.

AI tools and agents can query business data safely, because access and metadata were designed for that from the start.

You will close the gap between “we have data” and “we can act on data” — through the architecture, primitives, and defaults you build.

This is a software engineering and architecture role first. You’ll write and ship production code, own the tests and CI around it, and operate what you build — designing the interfaces, libraries, and primitives other teams build on, with the versioning, backward-compatibility, and reliability guarantees that implies. Your first six months should produce running systems, not documents. If your recent work has been mostly diagrams, roadmaps, and specs, this isn’t the right fit.

You’ll work horizontally across Data Engineering, Analytics, Cloud Infrastructure, and Enterprise Applications as the technical reference point for how teams model, catalog, and expose data, and you’ll regularly lead cross-team technical initiatives.

What You’ll Own

Treat the platform as a product. Know your consumers — analysts, engineers, applications, AI tools — and where today’s experience falls short. Drive a roadmap measured on adoption, trust, and time-to-answer, and make the case for foundational investment with evidence of consumer need. Ship the shared primitives other teams build on top of — not one-off deliverables, and not starter kits that fork and diverge.
ML and AI as a capability. Ship the first governed features analysts can apply to trusted data products themselves: anomaly detection over metrics, forecasting, segmentation, natural-language query against the semantic layer. Build them as repeatable capabilities with evaluation, monitoring, drift and cost visibility from day one — not a portfolio of bespoke models. Design how AI tools and agents reach the platform (MCP or comparable) as a core interface held to the same query-safety and permission guarantees as any other consumer — not a side channel around the controls.
Solve the cross-store problem. Arlo’s data lives in systems that were never designed to be joined — DynamoDB for operational and device data, Databricks for analytics, plus Oracle EBS, Amplitude, and Klaviyo. Design the identity resolution, referential integrity, and consistency semantics that let a consumer trust a join across them. Define query-safe access patterns so a dashboard, application, or agent can’t overwhelm an operational store or quietly return a wrong answer — and a permission model that holds across systems with entirely different native access controls.
Architecture. On that foundation, design Arlo’s semantic and metric layer and the catalog, so business terms, metric definitions, and ownership are consistent, discoverable, and reusable. Define data product contracts — schemas, ownership, freshness and quality SLAs, access patterns — including what’s safe to expose to dashboards, applications, and AI tools.
Governance. Build metadata, lineage, and access-control models into the platform itself, so governance is a property of the system rather than a manual review. Define what “trusted” means for a data product at Arlo, and make that trust visible and checkable. Separate foundational investment from one-off requests, and partner with Data Engineering, Analytics, and AI engineering leadership on build-vs-buy and sequencing.

What You’ll Bring

AI and LLM systems. Production experience building with LLMs — retrieval and natural-language interfaces over structured data, context and prompt design, and the evaluation, guardrail, and cost controls that make them safe to put in front of non-technical users. Shipped and operated, not prototyped.
ML as a platform capability. Stood up from the ground up and made usable by people who aren’t ML engineers — feature definition, training and serving paths, evaluation, and drift and quality monitoring.
Lakehouse depth in production. Unity Catalog, Delta Lake, medallion architecture, Lakehouse design patterns — with metadata, lineage, and governance designed in rather than bolted on. We run Databricks; deep production experience on a comparable platform transfers.
Heterogeneous data integration. Production experience reconciling data across stores with different consistency models, key spaces, and access controls — identity resolution and referential integrity without shared keys, and query patterns that protect operational systems from analytical and agent workloads.
Enterprise data architecture. Dimensional and semantic modeling, master data and ownership models, data contracts, and taxonomy design across multiple business domains and stacks. Not a single-team data mart — something several consuming teams depend on.
AWS at scale. AWS data services (DynamoDB, Redshift, Glue, or equivalents) in production. Oracle EBS, Amplitude, Klaviyo, or similar enterprise and product-analytics sources are a strong plus.
Programmatic data access. Access control and audit design for non-human consumers, and familiarity with MCP or comparable tool-callable interfaces.
Depth and range. 10+ years in data engineering or data platform roles, including production ownership of systems multiple teams depend on.
Coding. Strong SQL and Python (or another general-purpose language), plus the testing, code review, and production ownership that go with shipping code other teams depend on.
Adoption without authority. A track record of getting a platform capability adopted by teams that don’t report to you.

Nice to Have

Data catalog and governance tooling (Collibra, Atlan, or similar).
A regulated or compliance-sensitive data environment.
Replacing dashboard and reporting sprawl with governed self-service.

Ready to help build the data foundation behind the next generation of smarter, safer homes? We’d love to hear from you.

new_jobs.description:
About Carrot:

Carrot is the leading global fertility and family care platform, built on intelligent care orchestration: the right clinical guidance, at the right moment, in the context of each member’s life. More than a thousand multinational employers, health plans, and health systems trust Carrot to support millions of members across 195 countries – from pre-pregnancy through menopause and major life moments in between. Carrot's comprehensive clinical program delivers industry-leading cost savings for plan sponsors and award-winning experiences and improved outcomes for millions of people worldwide.

Carrot is widely regarded as a defining force in healthcare innovation as a recipient of several top-tier awards, including Fast Company's 'Most Innovative Companies' and CNBC's '100 Barrier Breaking Startups'. The company is regularly cited by leading global outlets — including The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, NPR, ABC News, and Harvard Business Review — as a leading voice on digital health, the future of work, and family health. Learn more at get-carrot.com.
The Opportunity
🚀

Carrot is seeking a Sr. Manager, Data Engineering to lead our Business Intelligence data engineering function as it scales to meet, and anticipate, the needs of the organization and its clients. This is a senior player/coach role with a strong emphasis on strategic leadership, technical excellence, and organizational impact. You will lead and grow a high-impact team while remaining deeply hands-on in architecting and building Carrot's data infrastructure.
You will set technical vision, drive cross-functional data strategy, and ensure our data systems are reliable, scalable, secure, and aligned with business priorities. You will influence and execute on the long-term roadmap for Data Engineering within the Data Team, defining how we ingest, transform, govern, and expose data across the company, and partner closely with senior leaders across Product, Engineering, Operations, Analytics, and Go-To-Market functions.
Given the small-but-mighty nature of the team, this role requires someone who is comfortable operating at multiple altitudes: setting multi-year architectural direction, shaping team and org design, and still rolling up their sleeves to build production-grade pipelines when needed.

What You’ll Own
💼

In this role, you will:
Own the technical vision and roadmap
for BI data engineering, aligning it with company strategy and analytics needs.
Design, build, and review scalable ETL/ELT pipelines
and workflow orchestration systems, contributing hands-on production code in Python and SQL
.
Architect and optimize data warehouse models
that support advanced analytics, self-service BI, and operational reporting.
Establish and enforce standards for reliability, observability, testing, and performance
across all data systems.
Drive improvements in data quality, lineage, and governance
, including documentation and metadata practices.
Partner with backend product engineering teams to co-design production database schemas
and event models with analytics and reporting in mind.
Lead, mentor, and develop a team of data engineers
, fostering a culture of technical excellence, ownership, and collaboration.
Own team-level planning and execution
, including capacity planning, prioritization, and delivery across concurrent workstreams.
Translate ambiguous business and analytics needs into a clear, prioritized engineering roadmap
with measurable outcomes.
Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Analytics, Security, and Legal
to align on priorities, ensure compliance, and remove cross-functional blockers.
Evaluate and influence build vs. buy decisions
, vendor selection, and tool adoption across data platforms, ingestion, and transformation.

What Success Looks Like
 📈

In your first 12–18 months, you will have:
Elevated the maturity and consistency
of data engineering practices across the BI function, with clear standards for reliability, testing, and observability.
Built and retained a high-performing data engineering team
recognized as a trusted partner to stakeholders across the business.
Delivered a prioritized data engineering roadmap
aligned with company strategy, with measurable progress on scalability and platform modernization.
Strengthened the accuracy, recency, and security
of enterprise data, meeting the requirements of regulated healthcare contexts.
Enabled advanced analytics, self-service BI, and data products
that drive meaningful business outcomes and influence Carrot's long-term data architecture strategy.

About You
✨

You likely have:
8-10+ years

of experience in data engineering or a closely related field, including 3-5+ years
leading and managing data or software engineers.
5+ years of advanced SQL

and 5+ years of Python development
experience in production environments, including unit and integration testing.
Strong, hands-on experience designing, building, and maintaining end-to-end ETL/ELT pipelines
in production.
Proficiency with cloud-based data platforms
(e.g., Snowflake, AWS) and modern ingestion, transformation, and orchestration tools (e.g., Fivetran, dbt, Prefect, Airflow).
Strong understanding of relational modeling and warehouse design principles
, plus version control (Git preferred) and modern CI/CD practices.
Demonstrated ability to define technical strategy and standards
while remaining capable of direct technical execution.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
, with strong knowledge of data governance, security best practices, and compliance protocols.

Nice to Have
⭐

While not required, we would be especially excited if you bring:
Direct experience with Carrot's current tech stack
: Snowflake, Fivetran, dbt, Prefect, and AWS.
Experience with enterprise BI platforms
and enabling self-service analytics.
Experience integrating batch and event-streaming or real-time ingestion systems
.
Prior experience leading data engineering teams in a startup or high-growth environment
, ideally including managing other leads or senior-level ICs.
Healthcare industry experience

, including familiarity with healthcare data standards (HL7, FHIR) and privacy regulations (HIPAA, GDPR).

Why This Role Matters
🧡

The reliability, scalability, and usability of Carrot's data systems directly power decision-making across the organization and for our clients. Data Engineering plays a foundational role in enabling the broader Business Intelligence function, and this role serves as the senior-most manager directly responsible for that capability.
The Business Intelligence team at Carrot is highly cross-functional and central to the company's long-term success. Led by our Vice President of Data and Business Intelligence, the team includes data engineers, data scientists, and business intelligence analysts. In this role, you will build and nurture a high-performing team, ensure the accuracy and security of enterprise data in a regulated healthcare context, and influence the long-term data architecture and platform strategy at Carrot.

Interview Process
🤝

We believe in a thoughtful and transparent interview process designed to create alignment for both candidates and our team.
For this role, candidates can expect:
Recruiter Screen — 30 minutes
Hiring Manager Interview — 30–45 minutes
Cross-Functional Panel Interviews — 45 minutes
Executive Leadership Conversation — 30 minutes
Hiring Manager Wrap-Up — 15 minutes

Throughout the process, we will share additional context about the team, business priorities, customer landscape, and what success looks like in this role.
  Why Candidates Join Carrot 🌍
Carrot offers the opportunity to do meaningful work in service of a deeply human mission.
Highlights include:
A mission-driven company focused on expanding access to fertility and family-forming care globally.
A high-growth environment where leaders are empowered to shape strategy and drive impact.
Competitive compensation, equity, and comprehensive benefits.
Flexible Time Off and a culture that actively encourages employees to recharge.
Comprehensive parental leave and family-forming benefits.
A collaborative, inclusive, and values-driven culture.
The opportunity to work alongside passionate, thoughtful teammates committed to improving healthcare outcomes worldwide.

Compensation: 

Carrot offers a holistic Total Rewards package designed to support our employees in all aspects of their life inside and outside of work, including health and wellness benefits, retirement savings plans, short- and long-term incentives, parental leave, family-forming assistance, and a competitive compensation package. The starting base salary for this position will range from $170,000-$210,000. Actual compensation may vary from posted base salary depending on your confirmed job-related skills and experience. 

Fraud and Security Notice:
Please note that all communication regarding job opportunities at Carrot will come exclusively from an @get-carrot.com email address. If you receive messages from any other domain, please disregard them and report the incident to: securityreporting@get-carrot.com

A Note on AI

At Carrot, we believe AI can help us work smarter, move faster, and create more meaningful experiences for our members, customers, and each other. While not every role requires deep technical AI expertise, we value people who are curious, eager to learn, and excited to thoughtfully incorporate AI into their day-to-day work.
For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement—and we'll call that out clearly in the qualifications. For everyone else, we're looking for people who embrace new ways of working, use AI responsibly to improve quality and efficiency, and continue to learn as the technology evolves.

Carrot has received national and international recognition for its pioneering work, including Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies and World Changing Ideas, Inc. Power Partners, and Modern Healthcare’s Innovators. Carrot’s global workforce has been acknowledged with several accolades, including Fortune’s Best Workplaces in Healthcare, Great Place to Work, and Age-Friendly Employer certifications. Job Title: Head of Software Engineering, Sr. Director
(hybrid- Monday- Thursday onsite )

Location:
US-GA-Atlanta (Sandy Springs)

: Exempt

About Safe-guard Products International

Safe-Guard Products International is the industry leader in automotive protection products and F&I solutions, partnering with the world's top OEM brands and a nationwide network of franchised and independent dealerships. Our platforms power the full lifecycle of vehicle protection—from dealer enrollment and incentive management to real-time rating, quoting, contracting, claims adjudication, cancellations, and consumer-direct experiences. We are transforming into an AI-first future culture, embedding intelligence across every platform our dealers, OEM partners, and internal operations teams rely on daily.

As we accelerate AI transformation, we are seeking a proven Head of Software Engineering to lead the engineering organization responsible for our client-facing and internal operations platforms. This is a career-defining opportunity for a technology leader who has built AI-native engineering cultures, delivered AI-powered platforms in complex regulated industries, and knows how to win in both the automotive and insurance environments.

Role Overview

The Head of Software Engineering owns software engineering strategy and execution across Safe-Guard's core platform portfolio. You will lead a multi-team engineering organization that builds and operates the systems underpinning dealer enrollment, incentive programs, rating, quoting, and remitting workflows, claims adjudication, cancellations, payment processing, and direct-to-consumer product experiences. You will partner with Sales, Key Partner Management, Operations, and executive leadership to align engineering capacity and roadmaps with company strategy, and you will help champion Safe-Guard's vision of AI-native software development, operationalizing the use of Claude, Cursor, and similar LLMs and software tools across engineering teams.

Note : This role does not have responsibility for ERP / Financial Systems or Business Analytics / BI reporting platforms.

What You Will Do

Engineering Leadership & Team Development

Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing software engineering organization across multiple product domains, client-facing dealer and OEM platforms, internal operations systems, and direct-to-consumer applications.
Own recruiting, hiring, and retention of top engineering talent; build career progression that reward technical excellence and leadership growth at every level.
Establish and sustain a culture of ownership, accountability, and continuous learning for engineers do their best work.
Conduct regular 1:1s, performance reviews, and career development conversations; actively develop direct reports into future leaders.
Partner with HR and Talent Acquisition to strengthen Safe-Guard's employer brand within the software engineering community.

Platform Ownership & Technical Strategy

Own the engineering roadmap and outcomes for Safe-Guard's client-facing platforms (dealer enrollment, rating, quoting, contract remittance, incentive management, direct-to-consumer) and internal platforms (claims adjudication, cancellations, and payments).
Define and help drive the technical architecture strategy, balancing modernization, and scalability, across a portfolio of applications serving automotive and insurance workflows.
Partner with Sales, Product Management, and Operations to translate business objectives into executable technical roadmaps, ensuring alignment between engineering capacity and company priorities.
Drive continuous improvement in system reliability, performance, and security; establish engineering standards for code quality, testing, observability, and incident response.
Make sound architectural and build/buy/partner decisions, clearly communicating trade-offs to senior leadership and stakeholders.

AI-Native Culture & Platform Development

Help champion Safe-Guard's AI vision by embedding AI-assisted development practices as standard practice across all engineering teams.
In collaboration with technology leadership, help design and delivery of AI-native platform capabilities, including intelligent automation in claims adjudication, contract processing, rating workflows, and dealer-facing experiences.
Build a team culture where engineers default to AI-first thinking: leveraging AI to accelerate development velocity, improve code quality, reduce operational work, and expand product capabilities.
Stay current on AI tooling and agentic AI approaches; bring informed recommendations to the technology and product leadership on emerging capabilities applicable to Safe-Guard's platforms.
Establish evaluation frameworks and responsible-use guidelines ensuring AI capabilities deployed in production meet Safe-Guard's quality, compliance, security, and reliability standards.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement

Serve as the primary engineering voice in executive and cross-functional forums; communicate technical strategy, progress, risks, and trade-offs clearly to both technical and business stakeholders.
Partner with Operations, Compliance, and Legal teams to ensure platforms meet the regulatory requirements of automotive and insurance administration.
Collaborate closely with our dealer network, OEM partners, and Key partner executive teams to incorporate external feedback into the platform roadmap.
Drive alignment across peer technology leaders—Product, Architecture, Data, Security, and IT to deliver cohesive, integrated platform experiences.

Delivery Excellence & Operational Maturity

Own end-to-end software delivery accountability ensuring teams execute with predictability, quality, and a consistent sense of urgency.
Implement and refine delivery practices, release cadences, and engineering health metrics that give leadership clear visibility into team performance and platform health.
Drive operational excellence: runbooks, post-incident reviews, and a culture of proactive reliability over reactive firefighting.
Identify and remove organizational and technical blockers that impede team velocity.

Experience

WHAT YOU WILL BRING

15+ years of progressive software engineering experience, including 7+ years leading engineering organizations of 70 or more engineers across multiple teams and domains including offshore contracting resources.
Demonstrated success building and scaling AI-native engineering cultures to fundamentally transform how engineering teams design and build software.
Hands-on experience building AI-powered production platforms; familiarity with LLMs, agentic AI architectures, and practical integration patterns for regulated business workflows.
Direct experience with AI-assisted development tooling including Anthropic's Claude, Cursor, and similar LLMs and products at team or organizational scale.
Proven track record in the automotive industry with direct experience working with dealer networks, OEM brands, or automotive F&I platforms strongly preferred.
Meaningful experience in insurance or insurance-adjacent domains (policy administration, claims processing, coverage rating and quoting, or similar regulated workflows).
Track record delivering complex, client-facing SaaS or platform products in a B2B environment where uptime, performance, and compliance are non-negotiable.

Technical & Domain Expertise

Strong command of modern software architecture patterns: microservices, event-driven systems, API-first design, cloud-native infrastructure, and DevSecOps practices.

Say hello to Hagerty

Hagerty is a company built by drivers for drivers. We put our members at the center of everything we do and are dedicated to making it easier and more enjoyable for enthusiasts to drive and celebrate the machines they love. We’re proud to be the world’s largest insurer of collectible and enthusiast vehicles and are home to the Hagerty Drivers Club, the world’s largest car club. Our Marketplace business presents live and digital sales across the U.S. and Europe, we host a number of driving events and concours, and our award-winning automotive journalists produce the most popular car magazine globally, alongside internationally awarded videos. We’re committed to Never Stop Driving. Ready to get in the driver’s seat? Join us!

As the Director of Software Engineering
in our Foundations Engineering
group, you will lead teams that are responsible for services that sit at the foundation of nearly everything we do. They include the creation, use, and management of digital identities, generation, storage and management of documents, acquisition and processing of payments.

As a director of engineering, you will have a small set of managers reporting directly to you. It will be your job to grow them and their teams in both technical and interpersonal skills as well as helping them deliver their work. You will also be responsible for effectively communicating, to technical and non-technical individuals, what your team is working on and any needs the engineering team may have. You must be deeply technical (e.g., still comfortable writing and reviewing complicated code), have strong communication skills, and the ability to develop and execute a strategy.

What you’ll do

Guide staff in delivering on the company’s long-term goals by:
Working with your manager to develop a nuanced understanding of the company’s goals and use that to develop a long-term strategy and quarter-by-quarter roadmap for your group.
Developing narratives that you, your managers, and engineers use to effectively communicate, understand, and keep salient the vision and strategy for your systems.
Participating in discussions on the feasibility of new capabilities, the cost to implement them, and the possible implementation timelines given current priorities and staffing.
Reviewing the design of capabilities, in conjunction with the architecture team, to ensure it is ready for your teams to work on and support your managers in explaining, breaking down, estimating, and delivering the work.

Influence and support the maturation of engineers and engineering practices by:
Participating in the creation and education of standards, practices, and idioms as well as reviewing the implementations of these things within your teams. This will require the ability to both write example code and review others’ code.
Helping to define and educate on what “quality” means for services throughout their lifecycle. This includes things like auditability, business continuity, deployment practices, documentation, maintainability, performance monitoring, testing regimes, security, and risk mitigation.
Developing, with the help of our legal and security offices, an understanding of the various auditing, compliance, regulatory, and security regimes (e.g., SOC, SOX, ISO27001/2) we must deal with and educating staff on their roles in those processes.
Educating engineering managers on the art of identifying and discussing the tradeoffs between various business interests, technical concerns, financial requirements, and more.

Develop a healthy and dynamic team that values and participates in the growth of individuals, the team, and the company by:
Developing practices for recruiting and hiring staff that bring in diverse thoughts and support their development of skills through deliberate practice, self-directed learning, and mentorship. This includes providing timely, candid, and respectful feedback on accomplishments and misses.
Coaching engineering managers on the differences between, and techniques for, managing individual contributors, peers, and superiors.
Coaching staff on core software development concepts, and appropriate application thereof, such as critical thinking, encapsulation, design patterns, and breaking/non-breaking API changes.
Developing qualitative and quantitative measures of team health and capacity used by managers to track, report on, and respond to their teams. Coach managers on how to use these measures to effectively manage team workloads, develop team members, and identify staffing needs.

Facilitate the collaboration within your teams and between your teams and the rest of the company by:
Collaborating closely with functionally related teams, product/business leads, and operations to ensure technology teams are delivering the company’s initiatives using the company’s processes.
Coaching managers on effective cross-team communication.
Supporting managers in identifying, understanding, and delivering dependencies other teams currently, or will soon, have on them and dependencies they have on other teams.

Monitor and improve the financial sustainability of your services by:
Developing, monitoring, and reporting on financial models (e.g., unit costs, run rates, cap/op expenses) for each service including new feature development and ongoing maintenance.
Supporting annual budget planning by providing cost-projections and well-reasoned investment plans based on the department’s strategy, vision, and expected growth. Monitor performance against plan throughout the year.
Educating staff on monitoring the financial health of their teams and services and working with them to develop methods for improvement.

Reliably identifies beneficial behavioral and organizational concepts, patterns, and principles and wisely discern when, and when not, to apply them across a variety of different situations.
Effectively communicates technical or abstract concepts to other engineers, technical and non-technical/business peers, your manager and their peers.
Consistently employs a decision-making process that allows you to identify and gather applicable data/facts, weigh tradeoffs, and mitigate any of your existing biases without getting paralyzed when working with incomplete information.
Experience in coaching individuals, with varying degrees of competency and differing communication/learning styles, in technical and non-technical skills.
Highly proficient with, and able to stay current on, the full development and deployment stack, e.g.:
Languages: C#, Terraform, Typescript

Operational Readiness: diagnostic and audit logging, metrics, tracing, monitoring, alerting
Deployment: VMs, containers, cloud providers, configuration management, canary deployments

new_jobs.description:
About Us

Hippocratic AI is the leading generative AI company in healthcare. We have the only system that can have safe, autonomous, clinical conversations with patients. We have trained our own LLMs as part of our Polaris constellation, resulting in a system with over 99.9% accuracy.

Why Join Our Team

Reinvent healthcare with AI that puts safety first. We’re building the world’s first healthcare‑only, safety‑focused LLM — a breakthrough platform designed to transform patient outcomes at a global scale. This is category creation.
Work with the people shaping the future. Hippocratic AI was co‑founded by CEO Munjal Shah and a team of physicians, hospital leaders, AI pioneers, and researchers from institutions like El Camino Health, Johns Hopkins, Washington University in St. Louis, Stanford, Google, Meta, Microsoft, and NVIDIA.
Backed by the world’s leading healthcare and AI investors. We recently raised a $126M Series C at a $3.5B valuation, led by Avenir Growth, bringing total funding to $404M with participation from CapitalG, General Catalyst, a16z, Kleiner Perkins, Premji Invest, UHS, Cincinnati Children’s, WellSpan Health, John Doerr, Rick Klausner, and others.
Build alongside the best in healthcare and AI. Join experts who’ve spent their careers improving care, advancing science, and building world‑changing technologies — ensuring our platform is powerful, trusted, and truly transformative.

Location Requirement

We believe the best ideas happen together. To support fast collaboration and a strong team culture, this role is expected to be in our Menlo Park office five days a week, unless otherwise specified.

About The Role

We are seeking a Director, Forward Deployed Engineering to own the technical strategy, integration architecture, and deployment execution that enables Hippocratic AI to launch voice-forward AI agents in. This is one of the most technically creative roles in the company - defining how agentic AI connects to customers requirements, and to the technical infrastructure within complex and security-conscious health environments. You will translate customer needs into Hippocratic agent technical specs and iterate with both the customer and the internal tech team on developing AI agents. You will design the integration of Hippocratic agents with customer CRM ecosystems, data lakes, and API architectures, working within their data governance frameworks and IT approval processes. You will own the agent script development, integration architecture, technical approval playbooks, and deployment operations that translate signed enterprise contracts into live, production-grade implementations. You will grow and develop a talent-dense team of Forward Deployed Engineers.

What You’ll Do

Customer-Facing Technical Leadership
Serve as the company's senior technical voice in customer-facing engagements — participating in enterprise sales cycles, technical workshops, and architecture reviews with pharma IT, security, and data teams.
Support Sales during RFP and RFI processes by providing accurate, compelling technical responses that demonstrate the platform's integration maturity and deployment readiness.
Lead technical discovery sessions with customer IT teams during the sales process — assessing integration requirements, identifying technical risks, defining deployment scope, and building the technical implementation plan that accompanies the commercial proposal

Customer AI Agent Development
Drive the translation of customer use case requirements into technical specs for AI agent development, from discovery through to UAT
Develop best practices for productive and rapid iteration and comprehensive testing of AI agent scripts. Maintain a continuous improvement playbook for script development that can be leveraged across customer engagements
Partner with Engineering to define AI agent building capabilities, integration platform capabilities, and technical infrastructure investments needed to support new customers

Integration Strategy, Technical Architecture and Security
Develop reference integration architectures for the platform's core deployment patterns, including integrations with CRM systems (Ex: Veeva, Salesforce Health Cloud), EHR (Ex: Epic, Cerner/Oracle Health), contact center and telephony platforms (Genesys, Five9, Amazon Connect, Twilio), and enterprise data lakes.
Design reliable and secure API-first integration patterns including REST APIs, webhooks, batch and real-time data synchronization
Working closely with the Hippocratic AI CISO, own the end-to-end process for navigating pharma IT security reviews, vendor qualification, and technical approval processes — building the documentation, processes, and institutional knowledge that make each subsequent approval faster.
Define and operationalize a repeatable deployment methodology for implementations — covering environment provisioning, integration configuration, data migration, testing protocols, UAT, go-live, rollback procedures and production monitoring. Oversee early deployments hands-on

What You Bring

Must‑Have:

Bachelor's degree or higher in a technical discipline (Computer Science, Engineering, Health Informatics, or Life Sciences). Advanced degrees or certifications in cloud architecture, or enterprise integration are a plus.
10+ years of experience in enterprise technical integration, forward deployment operations, solution engineering, or technical consulting in enterprise environments, preferably in healthcare.
5+ years of experience building and managing a team of forward deployment or integration engineers.
Strong technical fluency across API design and integration patterns and cloud infrastructure.
Demonstrated ability to engage credibly with enterprise CTOs, CISOs, enterprise architects, and IT governance teams — speaking their language and addressing their concerns with technical precision.
Comfort working in high-growth environments with limited structure, ambiguous requirements, fast pace, and high expectations for ownership, technical leadership, and cross-functional collaboration.

Nice‑to‑Have

Experience deploying AI, machine learning, conversational AI, or NLP platforms into enterprise environments.
Direct experience navigating enterprise IT security reviews, vendor qualification processes, and enterprise IT governance — including SOC 2, HIPAA technical safeguards, SIG questionnaires, and CISO-level security evaluations.
Hands-on knowledge of IT ecosystems including CRM platforms (Veeva, Salesforce Health Cloud), specialty pharmacy and hub systems, EHR systems, contact center platforms, safety databases, and enterprise data infrastructure.
Experience building and leading technical deployment or integration engineering teams.
Startup or early-stage company experience

Through evidence-based programs, advocacy, and public education, Shatterproof works to transform systems for tomorrow, support families today, and end stigma forever. Learn more at shatterproof.org.

Who Succeeds at Shatterproof

Shatterproof is in a period of transformative and rapid growth. We are building new systems, reimagining how work gets done, and creating more cross-functional alignment to accelerate our mission.

To thrive here, you should be energized by building, not just maintaining, and excited to bring structure, clarity, and innovation to evolving spaces.

We're Looking For Team Members Who

Build systems and processes from the ground up and improve them continuously as we scale.
Take ownership and act with a builder's mindset, bringing forward solutions rather than waiting for direction.
Influence and collaborate across teams, shaping work through strong communication and relationship-building.
Move quickly, learn fast, and adapt with resilience, especially in a high-growth, high-impact environment.
Are mission-driven and motivated to leave their mark on an organization working to reverse the addiction crisis.

The RoleReporting to the Chief Financial & Administrative Officer, the Vice President, Technology & Digital Strategy serves as Shatterproof's senior technology executive and leads the organization's technology, digital operations, cybersecurity, data, artificial intelligence, enterprise applications, digital platforms, and technology-enabled products.

This leader will create and execute a comprehensive technology vision that advances organizational strategy, enables operational excellence, strengthens security and resilience, improves the employee experience, supports fundraising and advocacy, and drives innovation across mission-focused platforms.

This role is ideal for a builder who wants the rare opportunity to shape not only an organization's technology strategy, but also how technology, data, AI, and digital platforms accelerate mission impact at scale.

The Team

The Vice President leads a multidisciplinary team spanning enterprise technology, digital operations, data, and product management. Current direct reports and functional oversight areas include IT Operations, Digital Operations, enterprise CRM and database capabilities, Treatment Atlas Product Management, and Treatment Atlas Data Management. The role is responsible for developing these capabilities into a cohesive, high-performing technology function that provides exceptional organizational support while advancing Shatterproof's digital, data, and platform strategy.

The team supports and manages a broad portfolio that includes enterprise technology and workplace operations, cybersecurity and privacy, Salesforce and enterprise applications, website and fundraising technology, business intelligence and reporting, artificial intelligence initiatives, and the current and future technology architecture supporting Treatment Atlas.

In addition to leading the internal team, the Vice President oversees a network of managed service providers, software vendors, implementation partners, and technology consultants, ensuring that internal and external resources are aligned to organizational priorities and positioned to scale with Shatterproof's evolving needs. This includes stewardship of strategic technology platforms and vendor relationships that support operations, fundraising, advocacy, data management, and mission delivery.

Enterprise Technology Leadership & Strategy

Develop and execute a multi-year enterprise technology strategy aligned with organizational priorities.
Serve as a trusted advisor to executive leadership on technology investments, risks, innovation opportunities, and emerging trends.
Establish technology governance, architecture standards, prioritization practices, and a transparent enterprise roadmap.
Evaluate and guide major technology investments, platform strategies, sourcing decisions, and vendor partnerships.
Ensure technology decisions support mission impact, operational effectiveness, sustainability, and growth.

AI Strategy & Digital Innovation

Lead Shatterproof's enterprise AI strategy and roadmap.
Establish governance frameworks, risk controls, and responsible-use standards for AI technologies.
Identify and prioritize AI use cases across fundraising, operations, impact programs, and administration.
Lead tool evaluation, pilots, implementation planning, adoption, training, and change management.
Monitor emerging technologies and assess opportunities to create measurable organizational value.

IT Operations & Workplace Technology

Lead IT and workplace technology operations for a distributed workforce.
Oversee managed service providers, help desk operations, devices, Microsoft 365, identity and access, collaboration tools, and general application administration.
Ensure timely and secure onboarding, offboarding, access management, and technology provisioning.
Maintain service standards, knowledge management, policies, procedures, and documentation.
Continuously improve reliability, support quality, and the employee technology experience.

Cybersecurity, Privacy & Organizational Resilience

Lead enterprise cybersecurity strategy, policies, governance, and training.
Oversee risk assessments, incident response, cyber insurance requirements, Keeper governance, backups, disaster recovery, and business continuity planning.
Partner with leaders to protect organizational, employee, donor, constituent, and program data.
Monitor emerging risks and drive practical, prioritized mitigation plans.

Digital Platforms, Website & Fundraising Technology

Lead the strategy, governance, performance, accessibility, analytics, and integrations for Shatterproof's website and digital engagement ecosystem.
Oversee fundraising and advocacy technologies, including DonorDrive and New Mode, and related digital vendors.
Partner with Development, Marketing & Communications, and Public Affairs to strengthen constituent experience, engagement, and platform value.

Salesforce & Enterprise Applications

Data, Analytics & Business Intelligence

Director of Software Engineering

About Safe-guard Products International

Safe-Guard Products International is the industry leader in automotive protection products and F&I solutions, partnering with the world's top OEM brands and a nationwide network of franchised and independent dealerships. Our platforms power the full lifecycle of vehicle protection—from dealer enrollment and incentive management to real-time rating, quoting, contracting, claims adjudication, cancellations, and consumer-direct experiences. We are transforming into an AI-first future culture, embedding intelligence across every platform our dealers, OEM partners, and internal operations teams rely on daily.

As we accelerate AI transformation, we are seeking a proven Director of Software Engineering to lead engineering delivery across our dealer- and OEM-facing enrollment, incentives, reporting, contracting, rate configuration, user management, and role-based access control platforms. This is an opportunity for an experienced, hands-on engineering leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment, champions AI-native development practices, and can operate as a credible technical partner to both business stakeholders and external clients in the automotive and insurance space.

Role Overview

The Director of Software Engineering owns engineering delivery, technical direction, and team leadership for Safe-Guard's externally facing enrollment, incentives, reporting, contracting, rate configuration user management, and role-based access control platforms. You will lead a team of approximately 20 engineers—including full-time employees and contractors—building and operating the systems that dealers and OEM partners rely on daily. Reporting to the Head of Software Engineering, you will partner with Product Management, Operations, and business stakeholders to align your team's roadmap with company priorities, while championing Safe-Guard's AI-native development vision, including the use of Claude, Cursor, and similar tools, across your engineering team.

What You Will Do

Engineering Leadership & Team Development

Lead, mentor, and develop a team of approximately 20 engineers (full-time employees and contractors) across enrollment, incentives, reporting, contracting portals, and rate configuration platforms.
Own hiring, onboarding, and retention of engineering talent; build career progression that rewards technical excellence and leadership growth.
Establish and sustain a culture of ownership, accountability, and continuous learning where engineers do their best work.
Conduct regular 1:1s, performance reviews, and career development conversations; develop future technical leads and senior engineers.
Partner with HR and Talent Acquisition to support recruiting efforts and strengthen the team's reputation within the engineering community.

Platform Ownership & Technical Strategy

Own the engineering roadmap and delivery outcomes for Safe-Guard's enrollment, incentives, reporting, contracting, and rate configuration platforms.
Define and drive technical architecture strategy across the platform portfolio (Angular, NestJS, AWS, Okta/OIDC), balancing modernization and scalability in a fast-moving, client-facing environment.
Define and own the user management and role based access control strategy across dealer-facing platforms, ensuring dealers and OEM partners can self-service user provisioning and access control within compliant guardrails.
Partner with Product Management, Operations, and business stakeholders to translate requirements into executable technical roadmaps.
Drive continuous improvement in system reliability, performance, and security; establish engineering standards for code quality, testing, observability, and incident response.
Make sound architectural and build/buy decisions, clearly communicating trade-offs to the Head of Software Engineering and other stakeholders.

AI-Native Culture & Platform Development

Champion Safe-Guard's AI-first vision by embedding AI-assisted development practices, including Claude and Cursor, as standard practice across your team.
Collaborate with the Head of Software Engineering and technology leadership to design and deliver AI-native capabilities across enrollment, incentives, reporting, contracting, and rating workflows.
Build a team culture where engineers default to AI-first thinking: leveraging AI to accelerate development velocity, improve code quality, and expand platform capabilities.
Stay current on AI tooling and agentic AI approaches; bring informed recommendations to technology leadership on capabilities applicable to your platforms.
Help ensure AI capabilities deployed to production meet Safe-Guard's quality, compliance, security, and reliability standards.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement

Serve as the primary technical point of contact for your platforms in both internal and client-facing conversations, translating complex technical topics for non-technical stakeholders.
Partner with Operations, Compliance, and Legal teams to ensure your platforms meet the regulatory requirements of automotive and insurance administration.
Collaborate directly with the dealer network, OEM partners, and Key Partner teams to incorporate external feedback into the platform roadmap.
Align with peer engineering and technology leaders to deliver cohesive, integrated platform experiences.

Delivery Excellence & Operational Maturity

Own end-to-end delivery accountability for your team, ensuring predictable, high-quality releases in a fast-paced environment.
Implement and refine delivery practices, release cadences, and engineering health metrics that give leadership clear visibility into team and platform health.
Drive operational excellence: runbooks, post-incident reviews, and a culture of proactive reliability over reactive firefighting.
Identify and remove organizational and technical blockers that impede team velocity.

Experience

WHAT YOU WILL BRING

10+ years of progressive software engineering experience, including 4+ years leading engineering teams.
Experience managing a team of roughly 20 engineers, including a mix of full-time employees and contractors.
Demonstrated success building AI-native engineering practices and embedding AI-assisted development (Claude, Cursor, or similar tools) into daily workflows.
Track record delivering client-facing, externally facing platforms in a fast-paced B2B SaaS environment.
Automotive industry experience—dealer networks, OEM brands, or automotive F&I platforms—strongly preferred.
Experience in insurance or insurance-adjacent domains (rating, quoting, contracting, or similar regulated workflows) is a plus.

Technical & Domain Expertise

Full-stack proficiency across Angular (frontend) and NestJS (backend), with a strong understanding of enterprise architecture and microservices patterns.
Hands-on experience with AWS cloud infrastructure, including container orchestration (e.g., ECS Fargate).
Deep understanding of Okta and OIDC/PKCE authentication flows.
Experience designing and operating user management and role-based access control (RBAC) systems across dealer platforms, including provisioning, permission modeling, and delegated administration for dealer network users.
Strong command of the full software development lifecycle: CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, code quality standards, and production observability.
Understanding of the regulatory and compliance landscape relevant to automotive protection products and insurance product administration is a plus.

Leadership & Communication

Proven ability to operate as a client- and business-facing technical expert, translating complex technical concepts into clear guidance for non-technical stakeholders.
Comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment with shifting priorities and competing demands.
Strong track record building trust with both internal teams and external partners, including dealers and OEM brands.
High emotional intelligence; skilled at navigating organizational complexity and leading through change.
Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field required; equivalent experience will be considered.

What Success Looks Like

In your first 90 days, you will have built strong relationships with your engineering team, Product partners, and key business stakeholders; completed a candid assessment of your platforms' health, team capabilities, and delivery practices; and established your presence as a trusted, decisive leader within the Technology organization. Within 6 months, your team will be operating with measurably improved delivery predictability, AI-assisted development will be embedded in daily engineering workflows, and you will have a clear roadmap for advancing your platforms' capabilities, and a unified user management model will be in place across all dealer platforms. At one year, your team will reflect your leadership: higher engineering velocity, strong dealer and client satisfaction with your platforms, AI-powered capabilities in production, and an engineering culture where the best people want to stay and grow.
